item.title: Trump Pauses Canada Tariffs for Three Days Subject to a Deal
item.description: The Trump administration agreed to delay 50% tariffs on billions of dollars of Canadian products for three days following high-stakes negotiations in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Australia’s Albanese Thanks Thai PM Anutin for Offer of Jet Fuel
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese expressed gratitude to his Thai counterpart Anutin Charnvirakul for an offer to supply jet fuel.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: South Korea Says Joint Military Drills With US to Be Curtailed
item.description: The US and South Korea agreed to curtail joint military drills after President Donald Trump ordered a reduction, citing his good relationship with Pyongyang.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Progressive Nixon Downs Vindman in Florida Senate Primary Race
item.description: Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon, a union organizer and Florida state lawmaker, clinched a surprising victory in the state’s Democratic US Senate primary, beating Alex Vindman, a former White House official who became a national figure during the first impeachment of President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Michael Smith

item.title: Trump-Endorsed Donalds Handily Wins Florida Governor Primary
item.description: Representative Byron Donalds won Florida’s Republican primary for governor, easily fending off a field of challengers after getting an early endorsement from President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Anna J Kaiser and Michael Smith

item.title: US National Debt on Brink of Passing $40 Trillion | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/18/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Republican Rep. Nicole Malliotakis of New York discusses her legislation aimed at raising the capital gains tax exclusion for seniors selling longtime homes. Kareem Crayton, vice president of the Brennan Center's Washington, DC office, raises concerns about the Justice Department's plan to deploy election monitors to polling sites. Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, says bringing down deficits is the "single most important thing" policymakers can do to improve affordability in a lasting way. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former DNC Chair Debbie Wasserman Schultz Wins House Primary
item.description: Former Democratic National Committee Chair Debbie Wasserman Schultz, a prolific fundraiser and a once-prominent messenger for the party, prevailed Tuesday in a congressional primary campaign marked by controversy over race and redistricting.
item.dc:creator: Emily Birnbaum

item.title: Lower Deficits Are Key to Affordability: MacGuineas
item.description: Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, says bringing down deficits is the "single most important thing" policymakers can do to improve affordability in a lasting way, arguing that heavy federal borrowing is putting upward pressure on inflation and interest rates. She also says there is a "huge mismatch" between politicians' warnings about the fiscal outlook and their willingness to embrace the higher taxes and spending cuts she says are needed to address it. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crayton Questions DOJ Election Monitor Push
item.description: Kareem Crayton, vice president of the Brennan Center's Washington, DC office, raises concerns about the Justice Department's plan to deploy election monitors to polling sites, saying questions remain about who will be deployed and the criteria used to determine where monitors are sent. He also weighs in on the Trump administration's push to obtain state voter-roll data and says there is little evidence of noncitizens voting in US elections, arguing such cases are "minuscule" when they occur. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Malliotakis Pushes Capital Gains Relief for Seniors
item.description: Republican Rep. Nicole Malliotakis of New York discusses her legislation aimed at raising the capital gains tax exclusion for seniors selling longtime homes, arguing it could make it easier for them to downsize and free up housing inventory. Rep. Malliotakis, who serves on the House Ways and Means Committee, also weighs in on the federal debt nearing $40 trillion and pushes back on concerns about the deficit impact of the Republican reconciliation package, arguing economic growth can help generate additional revenue. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: House Epstein Panel Chair Threatens Leon Black with Contempt
item.description: The chairman of the House committee investigating Jeffrey Epstein threatened to hold Leon Black in contempt of Congress if he fails to appear before the panel next month or doesn’t produce nondisclosure agreements the panel has subpoenaed.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly and Laura Benitez

item.title: Bolsonaro Names Ex-Energy Minister as Campaign Economic Adviser
item.description: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro announced a slate of new economic advisers Tuesday, including an economist and former minister who has published proposals for reining in the country’s rising debt levels.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Global Bond Slump Raises Fed Questions | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/18/2026
item.description: Long-term debt costs are soaring as the bond market slumps. Bloomberg's Chief US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey and Corporate Finance Reporter Davide Barbuscia explain why this jump is happening and what it signals to the Fed. Then, Empower Chief Investment Strategist Marta Norton on this week's global bond slump and how it's changing investor positioning. Plus, China Beige Book COO Shehzad Qazi previews next month's meeting between China's Xi Jinping and President Trump, and the future of trade between the two countries. Finally, Root CEO Alex Timm discusses how his company uses AI to help determine behavior-based car insurance. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy’s Popular Ex-Minister Calls for Ukrainian Election
item.description: The popular former Ukrainian defense minister, whose firing by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy triggered nationwide protests, strongly hinted at his political ambitions with a late-night video calling for wartime elections.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Verbianyi

item.title: Big Take Asia: North Korea’s New Economic Windfall
item.description: On the Big Take Asia podcast, K. Oanh Ha and Bloomberg’s Cat Barton unpack North Korea’s surprising rise from pandemic-era hardship to a multibillion-dollar windfall, and discuss how the country’s newfound wealth is reshaping geopolitical alliances in Asia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UAE Says Iran Fired Two Missiles at Country as War Drags On
item.description: The United Arab Emirates said that two ballistic missiles were fired toward the country from Iran, the Islamic Republic’s first known attack on the Gulf nation since May as the wider Middle East war continues unabated.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: US, Canada Talks Stall as Tariff Deadline Nears With Deal Unlikely
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration is downplaying expectations for a last-minute deal with Canada to avert fresh tariffs that are set to take effect Wednesday, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Alicia Diaz and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Trump Pick in GOP Florida Governor Race Byron Donalds Must Win Crowded Primary
item.description: Byron Donalds is holding most of the cards as Florida’s Republican voters decide who will be their candidate for the next Governor.
item.dc:creator: Anna J Kaiser and Michael Smith

item.title: Trump Chases Kim Jong Un Talks as Ties Fray With South Korea
item.description: President Donald Trump is pressuring longtime American ally South Korea over trade and security while, once again, making public overtures to Kim Jong Un.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi and Cat Barton

item.title: Trump Takes Iran Hard Line as Hormuz Tensions Set New Normal
item.description: US President Donald Trump insisted Tuesday that there were no talks ongoing with Iran, leaving the simmering conflict in the Middle East and control of the Strait of Hormuz stuck in limbo.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Patrick Sykes
